title: Self-contained proof of hook super-Schur formula s_{(a,1^b)}(q/u)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Sub-lemma G5.** Lemma `ef{lem:schur-1-1}` is currently delegated entirely to \cite{ChengWangBook}. For a self-contained solution, derive from the definition
$$s_\lambda(q/u)=\sum_{
u\subseteq\lambda}s_
u(q)\,s_{\lambda'/
u'}(u)$$
(single commuting variable $q$, single anticommuting variable $u$) that:

- $s_{(a,1^b)}(q/u)=q^a u^b+q^{a-1}u^{b+1}$ for $a\ge1,\ b\ge0$;
- $s_\varnothing(q/u)=1$;
- $s_\lambda(q/u)=0$ whenever $\lambda$ is **not** a hook.

**Approach.** In one variable, $s_
u(q)
e0$ iff $
u$ is a single row $(
u=(r))$, with $s_{(r)}(q)=q^r$; a single-variable skew Schur $s_{\mu/
u}(u)
e0$ iff $\mu/
u$ is a single column (horizontal-strip-free vertical strip), equal to $u^{|\mu/

This is a short computation (a few lines) but should be present rather than cited, to make the hook-coefficient extraction (G2) self-contained.

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Re-review against current draft — ADDRESSED.**
`lem:schur-1-1` is now self-contained: Fact A ($s_\nu(q)=q^r$ iff $\nu=(r)$, else
$0$) and Fact B (single-variable skew Schur $=u^{|\mu/\nu|}$ iff $\mu/\nu$ is a
horizontal strip) are derived from SSYT fillings with entries in $\{1\}$, and the
two surviving $\nu\in\{(a),(a-1)\}$ for $(a,1^b)$ plus the non-hook vanishing are
enumerated. I verified the resulting $s_{(a,1^b)}(q/u)=q^au^b+q^{a-1}u^{b+1}$ and
the non-hook vanishing against the Hilbert series ($n\le5$). No remaining gap.

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Verified: lem:schur-1-1 is self-contained and correct — resolving.**

I independently re-checked the current proof of `lem:schur-1-1`. It derives the hook super-Schur formula directly from the definition $s_\lambda(q/u)=\sum_{
u\subseteq\lambda}s_
u(q)\,s_{\lambda'/
u'}(u)$ with no computational reliance on \cite{ChengWangBook} (only the definition is cited, which is appropriate). The two ingredients are stated and proved from SSYT fillings with entries in {1}:

- **Fact A**: $s_
u(q)=q^r$ iff $
u=(r)$ (single row, $r\ge0$), else $0$ — exactly one column-strict {1}-filling exists iff every column has length $\le 1$.
- **Fact B**: single-variable skew $s_{\mu/
u}(u)=u^{|\mu/
u|}$ iff $\mu/
u$ is a horizontal strip, else $0$.

Combining gives the survival criterion: a term survives iff $
u=(r)$ is a single row AND $\lambda/
u$ is a vertical strip (conjugate of Fact B's horizontal strip). The three cases follow cleanly:
- (i) $\lambda=\varnothing$: only $
u=\varnothing$, value $1$.
- (ii) $\lambda=(a,1^b)$: $
u=(r)\subseteq\lambda$ needs $0\le r\le a$, and $\lambda/(r)$ is a vertical strip iff $a-r\le1$, i.e. $r\in\{a,a-1\}$, giving $q^au^b+q^{a-1}u^{b+1}$.
- (iii) $\lambda_2\ge2$: any single-row $
u$ leaves $\ge2$ cells in row 2 of $\lambda/
u$, so it is never a vertical strip; the sum is $0$.

**Numerical verification (sympy).** I implemented the super-Schur expansion via Facts A/B directly and confirmed: for all hooks $(a,1^b)$ with $1\le a\le3$, $0\le b\le3$, $s_{(a,1^b)}(q/u)=q^au^b+q^{a-1}u^{b+1}$; $s_\varnothing(q/u)=1$; and $s_\lambda(q/u)=0$ for non-hooks $[2,2],[3,2],[2,2,1],[3,3],[2,2,2]$. I also exhaustively verified the conjugacy fact used in the proof ($\lambda'/
u'$ horizontal strip $\iff$ $\lambda/
u$ vertical strip) for all $
u\subseteq\lambda$ with $|\lambda|\le6$.

No remaining gap; the lemma is rigorous and self-contained. No edit to solution.tex was required. Closing.
